name: phan
description: Phan is a static analyzer for PHP. Phan prefers to avoid false-positives and attempts to prove incorrectness rather than correctness.

latest_release.body:
Performance improvements:
- In the `'balanced'` `process_file_assignment`, also try splitting groups of files weighing more than half or a quarter of an even share (not only more than a whole share) and use the partition with the lowest predicted maximum load: a large class hierarchy that is under a share but placed first no longer leaves one analysis process noticeably heavier than the others (on a large codebase with `--processes 4`, the heaviest worker went from ~25 % above the mean to a few percent) ([#5601](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5601))
- Speed up the loading of plugins' return type overrides and function call analyzers, which took ~10 s on a large codebase before the analysis processes were forked: the inherited copies of a method are found by walking the subclasses of its class instead of grouping every method of the code base by its defining method, the internal callable-parameter checks are generated once per declared method instead of once per inherited copy, and the analyzer for plugins checking callable arguments is built once per declared method ([#5603](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5603))
- Add the option `lazy_inherited_methods` (off by default): the copies of methods that a class inherits from a parent class declared in a file excluded from analysis (e.g. a test framework) are created on their first lookup instead of when the class is hydrated. On a large codebase with many test classes this cut the wall time by 22-24 % and the peak memory of the main process by ~40 % with identical results; the verification mode `PHAN_LAZY_INHERIT_VERIFY=1` checks every lazily created copy against the copy an eager import would have made. Plugins implementing `AnalyzeMethodCapability` must also implement the new marker interface `AnalyzeMethodSkipsInheritedCopiesCapability` (their `analyzeMethod()` may then be called late, or not at all, for inherited copies that are never used); otherwise the option disables itself ([#5605](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5605))

Bug fixes:
- Keep the type of a variable unknown when it is unknown on some branches and known on others: `$x = null; if ($c) { $x = unknown(); }` (or the same with `try`/`catch`, `switch`, a loop, ...) used to make `$x` exactly `null` because the unknown branch contributed nothing to the merged type, so `PhanTypeMismatchArgument` (and related issues) were reported with certainty for a value that may be anything. The merged type is now `mixed` (resp. `T|mixed`), as the ternary operator already inferred in the same situation. This also makes the issues reported by `--processes N` runs less dependent on which process analyzed the callee, since a callee's inferred return type is only known to the process that analyzed its file ([#5602](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5602))
- Fix `PhanParamTooManyInternal` being reported for every call with arguments to 58 internal methods and functions that the PHP 8.2, 8.3 and 8.5 signature deltas listed with their return type only: the `Random\Randomizer` methods (`getBytes`, `getInt`, `pickArrayKeys`, `shuffleArray`, `shuffleBytes`), the `__unserialize` methods of the date, `SplFixedArray` and random engine classes, `Random\Engine\PcgOneseq128XslRr64::jump`, the PHP 8.3 `DOMNode` methods `contains`, `getRootNode`, `isEqualNode` and `replaceChildren` on every DOM node class, `IntlGregorianCalendar::setDate`/`setDateTime` and `curl_share_init_persistent`. The deltas now have the parameters, and a signature map entry without parameters no longer replaces the parameters known from reflection ([#5604](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5604))
- Fix the false positive `PhanTypeExpectedObjectOrClassName` for `new $x()` when `$x` has the type `object` without a known class, e.g. a `mixed` value narrowed by `method_exists($x, 'run')` to `class-string|object`: `new $obj()` creates an instance of the class of `$obj`, whatever that class is.
